The art is fantastic, the game has several unique spins on a farm sim/task management game, but oh. my. god. The time you spend walking is insane! And there's no in game way to improve it. Also very little way to track what you're doing. I don't need to be handheld but there isn't even a quest tab?? NPCs are only available once per week?? The fact that this game has been out for 7 years and they haven't fixed these very basic problems is atrocious. I genuinely thought this was in EA because of how many basic functions it lacks that would improve the game so much. I bought it for 90% off and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone for that price, save your money and buy a game that the developers care about.
It’s like Stardew Valley if Stardew didn’t want you to play the game. Every choice made is so hostile to the play and is incredibly unwelcoming. It’s a very frustrating game to play
Beat the main quest. Resource grind is ridiculous in parts and not being able to talk to critical NPC'S whenever makes the game more of a chore than it needs to be.

This game is a graveyard of unfinished ideas. Tons of mechanics that barely work, items that have no purpose, absent core game loop, etc.

Worst of all, devs knew about it and designed tons of time wasting mechanics to pad the game time as much as possible without barely any gameplay content. The late game is literally just skipping days waiting for RNG drops (required to finish the game) to happen.

It feels like early in the development this game had some original ideas but, instead of properly realizing them, devs decided to just release a half-finished product. Which, by itself, is somewhat understandable. But then they also released paid DLCs.

I really do not recommend playing this game past the first several hours. It just gets worse and worse.
Such a fun game - it is grindy and could use some QoL improvements but if you like crafting games and stuff like that then I highly recommend it. Best with all DLC...

This game is a whole lot more fun than I thought it would be. I assumed it'd just be another Stardew/Harvest Moon clone, but it's got some fun new mechanics, some morally grey choices and a really fun characters! I couldn't stop playing my first night. I stayed up wayyy too late.

Its fine.
Honestly I want to finish the game but every time I go to click play I remind myself of how much grinding I have to do just to progress, so I play something else.

Only issue I have is that I swear specific quests items for specific days spawn literally on the evening of that day and you have to wait an entire week to hand it in. Happened far too many times to be chance. It happened 5 times for sure and felt like the game was trying to extend the endgame chapters for me. But other than that, great game. Enjoyed it whilst chilling with Youtube on in the background :)

Total Grindfest for better or worse.

Game feels unfinished with secondary zones such as Fort and Town being hinted just off screen but not accessible.

Payoff for the grind is restricted to the pleasure of completing a grind, in game rewards/content never justifies the time spent to unlock it.

Automation elements are essential and completely frustrating to set up.

Its a bad game, made well.

It's good the first time around, then it's just a slog after that. It ends up requiring a LOT of needless grinding. And then there's all the content such as foods, status effects, and the red candle that was supposed to be usable in your church that just doesn't work. They were never patched, nor do I doubt they ever will be. On the surface, it's a quirky game. But then you realize it's a product that was released 85% finished.

It's a better, darker, less annoying, more fun version of Stardew Valley...

But with corpses, and witch burning, and reanimating the dead into zombies to make wine.

Too much based on Crafting for the sake of Crafting to keep the Player busy.
It feels more like Work, not like a fun Game.
- cut 3 Stones, sleep
- autopsy a Body, sleep
- dig a grave, sleep
You can eat to avoid sleeping, but sleeping is quicker and doesn't cost anything.
The Quests and Town Characters are not nearly as likable as in Stardew Valley.
All in all everything this Game does, does Stardew Valley a Ton better.

The art and its commitment to the theme are top notch. The game itself is fun initially but the resource management loop fails to feel rewarding. The game spirals so wildly out of control that your time in it seems to be a waste. I bought this because it seemed like a good game in the farming sim genre but in my opinion it does not provide a rewarding home base or reason to grind.

Edit: at the current price of free the game is absolutely worth a play.

Hmmm it's good, all nice, very addictive and interesting, but there are some mechanics that are annoying, but not enough to stop playing. Also some things have too many steps and it takes too much time to do, plus sometimes there is no in-game info about certain things or how to get them. Still, overall the game is good, I like it.

Graveyard Keeper is a smaller scale stardew valley with a lot of dark humor.

It is more "trial & error" oriented than the other similar games I played : few hints are given to the player to achieve the different goals, so you will mess up trying different stuff, but the game is pretty forgiving about that.

It feels rewarding to just try some goofy stuff and witness the world reacting accordingly.

Great alternative to a "Starvalley Dew" type game. Lots to do, upgrades, research. The whole thing with bodies, graveyard and church quality for success are a nice unique change of pace. The game revolves a lot around death, but it does it in a warm sort of way. Very peaceful game to spend time on.

As of the time of this review the game is free AND we will be getting the sequel some time this year (they say, you know how game dev can be). Let me be clear: there are no games that beat this one for what it is. Grab it while you can. Trust me.

The game is good, at least the first 15 hours I would say, but unfortunately the game starts to lose steam and the grind becomes just too much. And this is coming from someone who likes Old School Runescape. There needs to be more milestones and events that happen in between the grind to make it not feel so endless. This is a shame, as if the devs one day perhaps look at doing 'Graveyard Keeper Redux' where they revise and improve on what they have then this game could be really great. For the moment though, unfortunately I have to say that the game's grind just becomes too tedious. The game's charm and pleasing pixel graphics can not cover up for this.
A very fun, low stress game. Takes a while but I never feel too worried about completing objectives quickly. kinda grindy in the middle but a very engaging game all the same.

A highly addictive crafting/research casual game, with an elaborate tech tree, and a dark sense of humor. If you enjoy Minecraft, Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, or Animal Crossing, it will undoubtedly scratch your material grinding, resource organizing, and border-line obsessive-compulsive tendencies itch, nicely.

Mechanics within game are clever and intuitive which gives the overall game a great feel! Very little to exploit within game and you'll end up touching about 90% of the games' skills/crafts before completing the game which in itself is pretty cool.

Very long and slow and grindy game for the last few missions
had to wait 50 extra days to harvest skulls just to progress in quest

and gravekeeping is like 10% of the game

I would say , lovers of games like stardew, Bear and Breakfast, Terraria, littlewood and more look no further. This game does lack in certain aspects and can be confusing at times if you don't know what you're doing. It took me about 3 save files to really figure it out and still till this day there are things that i don't understand. Regardless of that this game has so much to offer including, decorating your base, farming, fishing, mining, zombie farms and specific quests that can only be done on certain days. The grind in this game may take some time but it definitely is addicting once you get the hang of it. 9/10. i do wish the tutorial was a little more in depth, just do your research and if you get stuck, there's always wiki! It may take place in a graveyard and your best friend may be a talking skull but the cozy aspects of this game are very present.

good at the start but slowly pads out each quest by making you wait weeks in game just to do it again, eventually taking what was good from the game and making it into a sort of idle game when all you have left is the last couple of quest. 6/10 Wish you could skip to the next day like stardew or something instead of swing your sword for a minute just for your character to sleep only like 1/3rd of the day

(Again not a "bad" game but definitely not my most favorite one unless you have a lot of time to spend and nothing else to really do : /

Great Game. There are a few picky things I had to adjust too but the good faaaaaarrrr outweighs the bad. Definitely recommend. The story is good, the crafting/building is great, and the interface is amazing. Lots of wonderful story twists and surprises. 9.5/10.

i've never played game with pixel graphics and rpg so this was a pretty new thing for me, but it turned out to be an excellent game, it's has a great story, funny dialogues, nice graphics, and the gameplay it's better than u could imagine, it's a must for anyone who likes playing alone

Oof, this game has pained me of slaving over hours just to get a lack luster of an ending. Not worth the time it took to even complete each mission. I wanted to see the town, the mountain fort, anything more than the same areas you go through a 1000 times. The ending was quick, sweet, but not enough for a game that filled itself with padding to make it last longer. Just watch a playthrough if you want to see what happens. It's not much.

What a surprise. I expected a small game with a bit of morbid humor, but it's much more than that. Captivating, much larger than I had assumed, and 11 hours play time in the what, 4 days I own the game speak for themselves.

I wanted to love this game, however a bugged autosave system easily backtracks DAYS in-game pretty frequently, also found a spot between a berry bush and a tree that traps the player. Lost all my progress

For an unfinished game (imo), I enjoyed it and will continue to play till I have nothing to do in the game.

Oh man, this game gives me that gameaddicting feeling, in both a good and bad way. It's basicly Stardew Valley simplified, yet more complex and tedious. If you have played Stardew Valley I would say, play this next! However if you haven't, I would recommend you to play Stardew first, then maybe pick this up on a rainy day. I score it 7/10 tombstones.
Edit: A few reviewers says its not comparable to Stardew because there's too little NPC interactions, I disagree. There are some NPC's that you can befriend (altough not as loveinterests), so listening to NPC's are still important - altough maybe NOT as critical as in Stardew. But if you ignore the NPC's the game will get harder.

TL;DR - Fun game at first, but feels like doing the chores later on.

Game starts of like most games - you don't know much, and have to do quests to learn and earn upgrades/unlocks to progress and plant yourself to operate independently. Slowly, the trend of "do X so you can do Y" repeats and repeats that it becomes a real chore rather than fun. I have to force myself to play it at times just to get by the initial point where it feels like I am about to do something laborious but in fact it is just a video game.

The "Graveyard" part is almost a side job after you've hit a certain point of the game, rather than a main element.

I believe it is appealing to some because of the Stardew Valley-esque aesthetic or somewhat gameplay (long walks to and from main town with single attack combat and relationship management with town folk); but it ain't for me.
The gameplay system was really confusing at first, but once you understand that, you'll be able to do a lot of things. Loved the massive chains crafting, source management, and the story.

Graveyard Keeper is a great game, but do not be fooled, it is an enormous grind.

I own all the DLCs and have earned every achievement. I have replayed the game multiple times, and several achievements are missable depending on story progression, so be prepared to plan ahead. As mentioned, the grind is real. If you enjoy min maxing like I do, aiming for perfect corpses and a fully decorated graveyard becomes a long term project. The Better Save Soul DLC in particular demands a lot with its requirement of 26 white skulls, and the basic automation in the game only helps so much. In the end you will still be limited by the sin shards you get from daily corpses.

The game is not difficult. You can take as long as you want to reach full completion. It is perfect for players who enjoy slow and repetitive progression. The start is quite slow, but things improve once you establish your automation. I would not call it groundbreaking, and there are a lot of quality of life improvements I would love to see added. Still, despite the simplicity and the long grind, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it.
very enjoyable game, can be overwhealming at first but the part i like most is there are no time pressure, you can do as fast or as slow as you like..
it's good but not great but still good. get if you are in to games like stardew but know that its still got some work ahead of it

If you're into management games like Stardew Valley you'll probably enjoy this, though it's not as deep. You don't really develop relationships with people, beyond them liking you more when you do them quest related favours. Just don't expect much from the story.

Pros:
- Unique, tongue-in-cheek concept works well
- Has some funny/shocking moments
- There's always a ton to do

Cons:
- The ending was disappointing
- Fishing felt like a chore, especially since I frequently found pressing to reel in a fish didn't register, resulting in me loosing both fish and bait
- There's nothing stopping you from doing things in unfortunate orders, or to suggest looking at something. For example, I unlocked the printing press near the end expecting it to help with writing, instead it only makes flyers I no longer need. Another example is experimenting with combat potions when you're most of the way to the bottom of the dungeon.

Verdict: 8/10

Very Recommended.

If your life takes an unexpected turn and the only way back is to be a good Graveyard Keeper, Will you be able to keep your morals in check? Or will you sell burger with mystery meat, Only for the profit it can bring? Don't let your self be fooled by the graphics, this game is darker then you think with some amazing story telling and a communist donkey ready to accept your carrots.

This game is way too fun, I get to live out my necromancer/ mad scientist dreams. I love the dark sense of humor, and the only thing that would make this better would be romance options. Cause why not.

It's definitely one of those: collect, craft, repeat until you can eventually start automating things, etc. But there's a lot of charm here, some decent story, and a decent dungeon combat system.
My one big complaint is that a lot of it feels like just worthless time wasting. Like the go back and forth quests or the resting until the right day comes about, which can take something like 5-10 minutes of just doing nothing, all pads out the length of this game to just much too long.

Very funny, pretty good balance between body parts/dead bodies but without being gruesome or gorey. All the characters ive met so far seem neat and have cool stories.

it's a bit of a struggle to remember what to do / how to get something after you read the dialogue, unless you're able to remember that stuff (im not) but thats where the wiki can help. or taking notes.

i really enjoy that theres no curfew like most games similar to this and I can stay awake for days straight if i want to/have the food to.

tldr; funny death game is fun

This game feels like a mobile game with roadblocks everywhere. After 10 hours of playing and looking forward to the fun part it just never got there. Cant drop Items, Quests aren't funny, just lacking soul everywhere.

Remember how Lord of the Rings Return of the King ended with Frodo? That's right. This is what I feel after finishing the game and it's DLC's. I am tired now, I think I go to bed for the coming week.

It's done.

The game is grind and a half, but I enjoyed the story enough to sit through it. You have been warned for the grind.

If you thought Stardew Valley was a little to intense in terms of time gating, but still want a fun and casual game with unique characters Graveyard Keeper is 100% for you.

There is LOADS of content, with lots to do and unique stories. If I had to criticize anything is that there is not always a clear 'how to do xyz' but, with some trial and error (or a wiki page) it is relatively easy to figure it out.

I LOVE THIS GAME. I played the entire story, and built most everything. The graphics are adorable, very pleasant to live in this strange, slightly creepy little world.

One addition it could use is a CREMATORIUM so the player no longer has to build individual biers.

I've not completed the game yet but here are my early takes:

Positive Stuff:
- Exciting story, interesting characters and funny writing
- Many (!!!) different mechanics none and of them feel weird / forced (farming, church and graveyard improvements, alchemy, writing, fighting through the mines, ...)
- Always something to do, improve and work towards
- Giant skill tree that (for me) makes progression feel rewarding

Negative Stuff:
- Beginning (first ~6h) is not (!!!) satisfying at all (you will run around a lot, figure stuff out and get lots of quests where you need A for B for C for D and the find out that you cannot even do D yet)
- Even though the progression is rewarding, it's still quite grindy (though the free Zombies DLC is supposed to help with that - I've just started with it though)
- With that many mechanics figuring out crafting materials and what is needed / used for what is tough (but you can check out the online wiki to mitigate that a bit)

I kinda had to force myself to keep playing through the first few hours but now I can't stop... xD

I played for about 5 hours, and am done with it. I agree with the other reviewers that it's a grindfest, and the overzealous nested build/mission trees drive me nuts (i.e. you have to chop down the tree to get the wood log to build the flitches to build the wood boards to build the whatever 4 more times deep, and combine that with 2 other things that also took that much effort to get what you ultimately need). It's also impossible to get blue tech points early on, i mistakenly used my first science points to research other random items instead of body parts so now i'm stuck and don't know how to dig myself out without starting completely over. It is a great looking game however, and i like the church service part of it which is unique, but even that has an annoyingly complex nested build tree to get better prayers. I also don't like how most NPCs are a store, that each sell like 2 things. And the early stamina issues are a big drag (i.e. running out of energy after crafting like 6 things, or chopping down 8 trees). Bottom line - If you are a casual player like myself, it's definately not the game for you. Try stardew instead.
One of the most addictive games I've ever played. Definitely some issues, but overall an indie classic.

Seems like a fairly decent game but I greatly dislike how I had to constantly refrence a wiki to verify things because I would constantly get stuck with no completable quest. Even now, I had to check a wiki to find out that to get a mixing station you need to stumble around blindly in the swamp until you find the middle.

Graveyard Keeper is a lot like Stardew Valley but with some light elements of automation and a more macabre tone. Despite the game's grim setting, it's quite calming, charming, and at times, funny. Characters are interesting and well developed, with distinct personalities and interconnected quest lines. In short, it's a relaxing game that manages to be engaging, fun, and even addictive--it's a great depression game!

My one gripe is that there a handful of things around the church that you cant fix. You can fix up *most* of the fences, but not all. It's a minor aesthetic thing, but it would've been more satisfying to completely fix up everything.

Complaints focus on the grind and the story, and recent reviews score 14 points lower than the all-time rating.
